key_insight: An uncertainty-aware framework translates patient risk predictions into ICU staffing plans that balance staffing costs against severe shortages.
clinical_relevance: The approach could help ICU planners anticipate staffing needs while accounting for rigid shifts and hiring delays.
method: Models dynamic predictive uncertainty without changing the upstream risk model.
Uses Conditional Value-at-Risk (CVaR) to assess extreme staffing shortage exposure.
Feeds risk-calibrated demand into hourly rolling-horizon staffing decisions.
evidence_signal: Evaluation on realistic MIMIC-IV trajectories showed a favorable cost–shortage trade-off versus deterministic and reactive baselines, with stress tests assessing robustness to calibration drift.
watch_item: Trajectory-based evaluation does not establish real-world staffing benefits or patient safety; prospective validation is needed.
paper_title: From Clinical Risk Prediction to Operational Decisions: An Uncertainty-Aware Framework for ICU Staffing
